sections.title: Ethnographic Research Methods
sections.description: A course in ethnographic participant observational research; its substantive orientation, literature, and methods. Emphasis is on the interpretive study of social organization and culture in educational settings, formal and informal. Methods of data collection and analysis, critical review of examples of ethnographic research reports, and research design and proposal preparation are among the topics and activities included in this course. Prerequisite: This course is designed to follow after Qualitative Modes of Inquiry (EDUC 682) and as such it is suggested that students have some background in qualitative methods before enrolling.

sections.title: Ethnographic Research Methods
sections.description: This seminar explores the epistemology, conduct, politics, and aesthetics of ethnographic fieldwork. In addition to examining classic and contemporary texts, students will gather and analyze ethnographic data. Participants will also navigate various phases of the ethnographic process, including gaining access to a research site or population, taking field notes, conducting and transcribing interviews, and performing preliminary analyses of their findings. We will also address the challenges associated with entering, being present in, and exiting the field. The seminar is therefore tailored for students who are eager to participate in focused, practical training in both ethnographic theory and practice. Also Offered As: SOCI 7468
